title: Chapter 5 financial application v3: contagion or interdependence across ex-ante VIX regimes
frozen_on: 2026-10-28, before any test statistic on these data was computed
question: After each industry's own GARCH(1,1) volatility is removed, is the joint distribution of weekly US industry returns the same in low-, medium- and high-VIX weeks?
returns: value-weighted daily returns (%), Friday weeks, 100 x sum of daily log(1 + r/100); trailing incomplete week dropped
regime: lagged VIX: Cboe close on the last trading day of the previous Friday week; terciles of weekly VIX in the presample period; 1 = low, 2 = medium, 3 = high

representations.raw: weekly log returns; benchmark, rejection expected because volatility differs by construction
representations.innov: GARCH(1,1) Gaussian QML innovations, one filter per industry fitted to the analysis period without labels (as in simulation E8)
representations.dir: innov / ||innov||, the direction of each week's innovation vector; invariant to any scale common to all industries in a week
representations.innov_pre: GARCH parameters fitted on the presample only, recursion forward (robustness)

primary.multiplicity: Holm over the two primary hypotheses
primary.benchmark: raw (reported, not part of the Holm family)

calibration_checks.placebo: ind30, innov and dir: the regime sequence is shifted circularly by 200 distinct offsets drawn uniformly from 52..(T-52) weeks (seed 20261029); the data and the block split are those of the main analysis; B = 199
calibration_checks.bootstrap_null: ind30: 200 data sets; innovation vectors are resampled with replacement from the main innovations (rows kept intact), returns are generated with the fitted GARCH(1,1) of each industry (burn-in 200 weeks), the filters are re-estimated, and innov and dir are tested with the real regime sequence and split; B = 199; seed (20261030, r) for data set r
calibration_checks.criterion: rejection rate at 0.05 with its 95% Clopper-Pearson interval; reported in full whatever its value

reporting: all p-values of all methods and settings are reported; one-versus-rest T statistics by regime and learner are reported for interpretation (Remark 7); economic descriptives by regime: mean pairwise correlation of innovations, absorption ratio (top d/5 eigenvalues of the correlation matrix), lower-tail co-exceedance at the 5% level, innovation variance, risk of the low-regime minimum-variance portfolio in other regimes
